manuscript_statement: The stability condition tau_T >= tau_q/2, often quoted as the stability condition of DPL thermoelasticity, was derived by Quintanilla [Quintanilla2003DPL] for the version in which the flux is expanded to second order in tau_q and the gradient to first order in tau_T, i.e. variant (ii).
cited_source: Quintanilla2003DPL | Quintanilla, R. (2003), A condition on the delay parameters in the one-dimensional dual-phase-lag thermoelastic theory, Journal of Thermal Stresses 26:713-721
source_page_or_equation: p. 713 (abstract); p. 714, text after Eq. (1) and Eq. (4); p. 716, Eq. (11)
source_wording_max25words: when tau_y > tau_q/2 the solutions decay exponentially and when tau_y < tau_q/2 there exist unstable solutions
what_source_actually_states: (the source prints the temperature-gradient lag as tau_y; the manuscript calls it tau_T) The paper takes the Taylor series on both sides of q(x,t+tau_q) = -k grad theta(x,t+tau_y) and keeps terms up to second order in tau_q but only first order in tau_y (p. 714), i.e. exactly variant (ii); Eq. (4) on the same page shows the two expansions. Exponential stability of the one-dimensional thermoelastic problem is then proved under tau_y > tau_q/2 (p. 716, Eq. (11)) and instability for tau_y < tau_q/2 in Section 4. The paper proves strict inequalities only and never states or tests the equality tau_y = tau_q/2, so the manuscript's '>=' form is not what the source establishes.

source_wording_max25words: We obtain conditions on the material parameters to guarantee the exponential stability of solutions
what_source_actually_states: The abstract states that the authors consider two cases of three-phase-lag heat conduction, propose a Lyapunov function for each, and obtain conditions on the material parameters that guarantee exponential stability, adding that when those conditions fail instability follows for suitable domains. Section 1 sets up the two equations (1.1) and (1.2) with the three lags and their first- and second-order truncations. So the paper does give stability conditions for TPL, which is the part of the sentence that rests on Quintanilla2008a; the end-effects half rests on Quintanilla2008 and is treated in CC-0002.
